# Data provenance — `test_run.jsonl`

**Status: SYNTHETIC (simulated).** Generated by `src/generate_data.py` with a fixed
seed (`numpy.random.default_rng(42)`): 12 warm-up + 150 evaluation runs for each of
2 methods x 3 platforms = 972 records. It is **not** a measurement of real platform
infrastructure and must not be cited as empirical evidence.

## Schema (one JSON object per line)

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `run_id` | int | sequential run identifier |
| `phase` | str | `warmup` (cold start, discarded) or `eval` (measured) |
| `method` | str | `baseline` (sequential collector) or `proposed` (concurrent collector) |
| `platform` | str | `TikTok`, `Instagram Reels` or `YouTube Long` |
| `latency_ms` | float | wall-clock time of the run, milliseconds |
| `throughput` | float | videos processed per second |
| `error` | bool | whether the run failed (guardrail metric) |

## Using real logs

Replace this file with real collection logs in the same schema and run
`python src/process_data.py && python src/visualize.py` (or re-run the notebook).
Everything downstream is recomputed automatically.
